0.title: Who We Invite
0.text: We invite students from transport universities and other technical universities who are interested in solving real industry problems.

1.title: Who This Is For
1.text: If you want to test yourself in conditions close to real industry work, apply your engineering skills, and learn something new — this is definitely for you. It doesn’t matter what experience you already have — what matters is the desire to understand complex situations, offer unconventional solutions, and do it with reasoning.

faq-items.title: Who can participate?
faq-items.content: Students of any year enrolled in higher education programs at transport and technical universities and obtaining their first degree can participate. Teams with diverse skills — from analytics and engineering to design and IT — are encouraged.

faq-items.title: Do I need a ready project to participate?
faq-items.content: No. All teams start from the same point — a problem description. You will develop your solution step by step during the contest.

faq-items.title: What will participants do?
faq-items.content: You will investigate a real problem of a transport company, propose a solution, build a prototype, and present it to experts. The process follows a classic project flow: analysis → idea → validation → result.

faq-items.title: Can I participate individually?
faq-items.content: No, participation is only possible as part of a team. Each team represents one educational institution and may include students from different groups and years.

faq-items.title: What has changed this season?
faq-items.content: This year, the final format has been updated and a project expo has been introduced — teams present solutions in an engineering fair format. More real industry challenges have been added, along with technical support and new tools. The international track has been expanded with teams from other countries.

faq-items.title: How many problems can a team solve?
faq-items.content: Each team can work on only one problem, and each participant can be part of only one team. The top 3 Russian teams and several international teams for each of the 6 problems will advance to the final.

faq-items.title: What do winners receive?
faq-items.content: The prize pool is 2 million rubles, along with gifts, diplomas, and most importantly — experience, connections, and new opportunities. Top teams may also be invited to future seasons and industry events.

1.title: Situation Analysis
1.subtitle: Analyze the current situation to understand the problem, identify key factors, and determine the stakeholders that should be involved in solution process.
1.text: At the first stage of the contest, you will use several tools. They will help you better understand the current situation, identify the key factors influencing it, and determine more stakeholders that should be involved in the project.

2.title: Problem Interview
2.subtitle: Conduct interviews with potential parties involved in the situation to identify problems, needs, and barriers that you should consider when developing the solution.
2.text: A problem interview is a research method used to better understand the target audience’s needs, pain points, fears, and objections. This step in the project helps avoiding the creation of a product that nobody needs as well as it is used to identify real problems of the audience, and to find effective solutions. You will need to find out the people who can provide important additional insights about the situation, contact them, and record the results.

3.title: Solution Idea
3.subtitle: Formulate an idea of your solution. Consider the results of analysis and interviews you have already performed and take into account key problems and needs of users of your solution.
3.text: At this stage, you need to develop a solution to the problem you have identified that builds on information from the previous stages. Structure the information as this helps organize insights and highlight the most promising areas for solution development. It is important to stay focused on the core problem and not to digress from it. As a result, you will form a clear concept of your solution that takes into account all key factors and proposes concrete steps to improve the situation.

4.title: Prototyping
4.subtitle: Create a prototype of your solution to clearly demonstrate how it works and the value it creates.
4.text: At this stage, you will refine and implement your solution. Firstly, specify all requirements for the future product. They must be well-formulated and measurable, so that you can build a prototype that works. The final step is practical implementation. Create a prototype, mockup, or concept of your solution. It is important to clearly demonstrate the current level of development of the project. The more detailed and well-defined your work is, the more points you get from the jury.

5.title: Video Presentation
5.subtitle: Present your solution in a video format: demonstrate the results and explain your decision-making process.
5.text: This is the final stage of your project work. You need to present results of your team in a video and in a final presentation. Your goal here is to review all materials you have elaborated during the contest and present them in a clear and structured way. It is important to demonstrate the logic behind your decisions and explain how your product solves the identified problem and integrates into the workflows of key stakeholders.

main-stage-initial-card-info.title: Welcome to the International Transport Project Contest!
main-stage-initial-card-info.text-1: Project work is a step-by-step process of working with a real problem: you are going to analyze the situation, independently find and interview experts, formulate an idea, create a minimal prototype, and record a video explaining how your workflow is organized and what results you achieved. The stages form a sequence of steps and each of them builds on the previous one, and that is why it is important to use the results from earlier stages.
main-stage-initial-card-info.text-2: You will be able to choose between three options to approach the task — basic, design thinking, and system thinking (with diagrams and models). Select one at the beginning, stick to it until the end, and change or combine tools only when necessary.
main-stage-initial-card-info.text-3: Plan your time: analysis, interviews, and formulation of your solution idea should take up to two weeks, so that there is enough time for prototyping and the final video presentation.
